audit: VERTEX Kattis candidate original-statement evidence ledger — pass 1
method: For each row, confirm the title/problem ID in an original contest statement copy or a statement hosted by the contest university; record its source URL, a short excerpt, input/output observations, constraints observations, and a scenario-depth note. This pass does not independently retrieve the live Kattis page, and statement identity does not itself qualify a problem as a long scenario.

records.title: Bank Queue
records.statementTitle: KTH Challenge 2013, Problem F — Bank Queue
records.identity: title and problem ID bank explicitly match
records.observed: The statement describes a bank queue, one counter, customers who leave at deadlines, and maximizing the cash served before closing.
records.excerpt: There are many people standing in the queue wanting to put cash into their accounts after they heard that the bank increased the interest rates.
records.inputOutput: Input: N, closing time T, and each customer's cash and leave deadline. Output: maximum cash served before closing.
records.constraints: N up to 10,000; T up to 47; per-person cash and deadline bounds stated.
records.scenarioNotes: Concrete queue and deadline context, but the task is a compact scheduling optimization; long-scenario depth remains a separate judgement.

records.title: Postal Delivery
records.statementTitle: ACM-ICPC 2016 Mid-Central Regional, Problem I — Postal Delivery
records.identity: title and problem ID delivery explicitly match
records.observed: The statement models a postal truck delivering letters to one-dimensional addresses, with limited carrying capacity and required returns to the post office to reload.
records.excerpt: It may be that all the mail to be delivered does not fit on the mail truck at once, in which case the distance traveled by the truck must include travel back to the post office to reload.
records.inputOutput: Input: N, truck capacity K, and ordered address coordinates with letter counts. Output: minimum total distance while delivering all mail and returning.
records.constraints: N up to 1,000; capacity up to 10,000; coordinates and letter quantities bounded in the statement.
records.scenarioNotes: Multi-stop logistics context with capacity, route direction, repeated trips and optimization. Stronger long-scenario candidate, but qualification is not yet formally approved.

records.title: Planting Trees
records.identity: title and problem ID trees explicitly match
records.observed: Farmer Jon plants seedlings one per day, each with a known growth duration, and wants the earliest possible party date after all mature.
records.excerpt: Farmer Jon has recently bought n tree seedlings that he wants to plant in his yard. It takes 1 day for Jon to plant a seedling.
records.inputOutput: Input: N and N growth durations. Output: earliest day the party can be organized.
records.constraints: N up to 100,000; each growth duration up to 1,000,000 days.
records.scenarioNotes: Official story is short and reduces to sorting growth times; unlikely to satisfy a strict long-scenario threshold.

records.title: Canvas Painting
records.identity: title and contest problem C confirmed; Kattis slug canvas corroborated by archive index
records.observed: Samuel's machine paints canvases in repeated steps: canvases are ordered, a color is split into two new colors at a chosen position, and ink cost depends on canvas sizes.
records.excerpt: His newest idea involves creating arrays of canvasses with color patterns having no repeated colors.
records.inputOutput: Input: test cases, number of canvases, and their sizes. Output: minimum ink required for all canvases to have distinct colors.
records.constraints: The statement contains explicit per-test-case input and canvas-count/size bounds; those bounds should be copied verbatim during schema enrichment.
records.scenarioNotes: Multi-step machine process with repeated operations and optimization; potentially a good scenario candidate. Formal depth decision remains pending.

records.title: Daydreaming Stockbroker
records.identity: title and problem ID stockbroker explicitly match
records.observed: Gina imagines using historical stock prices to trade whole shares, with a finite total share supply and no fees or market impact.
records.excerpt: Now Gina starts to wonder: if she were to go back in time a few days and bring a measly $100 with her, how much money could she make
records.inputOutput: Input: number of days and daily stock prices. Output: maximum final amount of money.
records.constraints: At most 365 days; price bounds and maximum 100,000 shares are explicit.
records.scenarioNotes: Narrative is memorable but compact and the underlying task is a one-pass stock-profit simulation; long-scenario status not established.

records.title: Marbles On A Tree
records.statementTitle: Waterloo Programming Contest, Problem E — Marbles on a tree
records.identity: title and full tree-marble problem statement match
records.observed: The statement defines boxes on a rooted tree, exactly n marbles total, and moving marbles across adjacent vertices until each vertex has one.
records.excerpt: The task is to move the marbles such that each box contains exactly one marble.
records.inputOutput: Input: multiple tree cases with each vertex's marble count and children. Output: minimum number of marble moves.
records.scenarioNotes: The task is primarily an abstract tree balancing problem with a concise framing; long-scenario qualification remains unassessed.

remainingWork: Continue original-statement retrieval for the other 35 candidates. Do not mark any candidate importApproved until identity, canonical URL, statement evidence, full constraints, input/output contract, and long-scenario quality all pass.
